message.name: ROSBOT_IMU
message.description: IMU sample (orientation + gyro + accel) from rosbot MCU.
message.field: Timestamp since MCU boot [us].
Orientation {x,y,z,w}.
Gyro [rad/s], IMU frame.
Accel [m/s^2], IMU frame.

message.name: ROSBOT_JOINT_STATE
message.description: Wheel joint state, order: FL, FR, RL, RR.
message.field: Timestamp since MCU boot [us].
Wheel position [rad].
Wheel angular velocity [rad/s].
Wheel effort [Nm or PWM duty fallback].

message.name: ROSBOT_BUTTONS
message.field: Timestamp since MCU boot [us].
Pressed-button bitmask.

message.name: ROSBOT_IMU_CALIBRATION
message.description: BNO055 calibration state, read live off the chip. The chip calibrates continuously in its fusion mode, so this rises while the robot is moved. MAV_CMD_USER_2 param1 selects the action: 1 start a session (red LED blinks fast until fully calibrated), 2 persist the current offsets (ends the session), 0 stop the session. save_seq/state report the outcome of the last save.
message.field: System calibration level, 0..3.
Gyroscope calibration level, 0..3.
Accelerometer calibration level, 0..3.
Magnetometer calibration level, 0..3.
Last save: 0 none, 1 saving, 2 saved, 3 rejected (not fully calibrated), 4 failed (I2C or flash).
Incremented each time a save finishes, so a host can tell a fresh result from a stale one.
1 when flash holds calibration offsets that are applied at boot.
1 while a calibration session is running.

message.name: ROSBOT_POWER_SUPPLY
message.description: Battery state that BATTERY_STATUS cannot carry. Sent right after each BATTERY_STATUS. On ROSbot 3 only design_capacity_mah is meaningful (status 0, charger_type 255, present 1).
message.field: sensor_msgs/BatteryState POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_* value reported by the power board.
0 none, 1 USB-C, 2 inductive, 255 unknown (not reported yet).
1 when a battery is connected.
Pack design capacity.
Full capacity learnt by the power board (ROSbot XL, PB firmware v1.0.5+), 0 = unknown.

message.name: ROSBOT_WHEEL_SETPOINTS
message.description: Wheel velocity setpoints, order: FL, FR, RL, RR.
message.field: Bridge-side stamp for diagnostics [us].
Target wheel angular velocity [rad/s].

message.name: ROSBOT_PANEL_LEDS
message.field: Desired LED bitmask.

message.name: ROSBOT_LED_STRIP
message.field: Number of valid pixels (0..18).
Pixel data, RGB triplets, count*3 valid bytes.

message.name: ROSBOT_MCU_ID
message.description: Reply to MAV_CMD_USER_1 carrying the MCU unique identifier.
message.field: Hex-encoded 12-byte MCU UID.

message.name: ROSBOT_POWER_BOARD
message.description: Reply to MAV_CMD_USER_3 carrying the version strings the ROSbot XL power board reported over its UART. valid is 0 until the board has answered, which is also the permanent state with a power board firmware that does not report it.
message.field: 1 when the power board has reported its versions.
Power board firmware version, e.g. v1.0.1.
Power board hardware revision, e.g. v1.4.

message.name: ROSBOT_DIAGNOSTICS
message.description: MCU and hardware health, sent once a second. Counters run since MCU boot and only grow, so a host compares them between messages.
message.field: Time since MCU boot.
Free heap now.
Heap never handed out since boot, a lower bound of the free heap.
Failed IMU reads.
Telemetry frames dropped because the link TX queue was full.
Incoming MAVLink frames the parser dropped (CRC or framing).
Cause of the last MCU reset, bitmask: 1 reset pin, 2 power-on or brown-out, 4 software, 8 independent watchdog, 16 window watchdog, 32 low-power, 64 firmware fault (fatalError).
CPU idle over the last report period, 0.1 % units; 65535 in the first message after boot (no period yet).
Smallest stack headroom of any task since boot.
Range sensor reads that timed out, order FL, FR, RL, RR (ROSbot; zero elsewhere).
I2C bus resets after faults: IMU bus, sensor/EEPROM bus.
Motor driver fault events (nFAULT asserted).
Times the bridge connection was (re)established.
Name of the task with the smallest stack headroom.
1 when the IMU initialised and its last read succeeded.
Bitmask of range sensors that initialised, bit 0 = FL.
Program counter of the exception that caused the last firmware fault, 0 if not an exception.

Why the last firmware fault reset happened: 0 none or unknown, 1 assert, 2 stack overflow, 3 out of heap, 4 hard fault, 5 memory-management fault, 6 bus fault, 7 usage fault, 8 NMI, 9 clock failure (did not start, or the crystal stopped), 10 libc exit.
Task whose stack overflowed (fault_code 2).
Bitmask: 1 battery low, 2 battery critical, 4 motor fault active, 8 power board answering, 16 Ethernet link up, 32 board has range sensors, 64 board has a power board, 128 board has Ethernet.
What clocks the MCU: 0 unknown (older firmware), 1 crystal, 2 internal RC oscillator because the crystal did not start.
